lines.en: The subway train stopped about halfway across Dongho Bridge.
A few survivors awkwardly got to their feet and looked outside. Seoul in ruins, and collapsed buildings.
Monsters resembling enormous snakes were tearing apart and eating the wreckage of a fighter jet that had crash-landed in the Han River.
“Wh-what the hell are those......!”
I recognized them at once.
Ichthyosaurs (魚龍).
Monsters commonly called sea serpents. They would later be classified as a grade 7 monster species in the world of ‘Ways of Survival.’
One of the ichthyosaurs turned toward us.
“A-aaah! It's coming!”
People cried out in terror. But even as I watched the ichthyosaur approach, I felt nothing. They couldn't pose a threat.
Grrrrrrr.
With a rumbling cry, the ichthyosaur circled beneath Dongho Bridge, then disappeared in a trail of bubbles.
In the world of Ways of Survival, ‘scenarios’ take precedence over everything.
So as long as we were under a scenario's protection, we wouldn't have to confront them right away. For now, at least.
[Reward settlement has been delayed by an unexpected scenario inspection. Please wait.]
Reward settlement should have begun by now, but the only thing floating in the air was an error message.
This was probably because of me.
I looked down at Kim Namwoon's corpse, of which only the torso remained.
If things had followed the original course of ‘Ways of Survival,’ Kim Namwoon should have killed most of the people in this carriage and moved on to the next scenario.
But I had prevented that.
If I was right, those enraged by Kim Namwoon's death would make themselves known about now. Here? No, not here. Up in that sky, to be precise.
[Two constellations express faint hostility toward you over the death of the character ‘Kim Namwoon.’]
Constellations (星座).
The most mysterious beings in the world of ‘Ways of Survival,’ and the forces behind the tragedy, seated atop distant nebulae (星雲), watching this entire story unfold.
Seeing the constellations' expressions of approval and disapproval (好惡) appear made it sink in that things were beginning in earnest.
It was funny.
Until just yesterday, our positions had been the exact opposite. Now they were watching me.
[A few constellations express admiration for your scenario.]
[The constellations donate 500 coins to you.]
If some of them disliked me, others were bound to like me.
Either way, the situation was equally uncomfortable, but there was nothing I could do about them for now.
I was the clown now.
As I picked up Kim Namwoon's Swiss Army knife from the floor, I thought.
Watch all you like. The price of admission will be your lives in the end.
“......Kim Dokja-ssi? Are you all right?”

I raised my head and saw Yoo Sangah's face. Drooping shoulders. Bloodstains scattered across her white blouse, and runs in her stockings. The Yoo Sangah I had known was gone. I took her hand and stood up, saying,
“I'm sorry. I couldn't save the old woman.”
I looked down at the old woman's corpse, which was also missing its head. An old woman whose name I didn't even know. Many more people would die like this.
Yoo Sangah looked at me with conflicting emotions in her eyes.
“Dokja-ssi, how can you be so.......”
“Pardon?”
“N-no, it's nothing. More importantly...... thank you.”
“What for?”
“Well, earlier.......”
A scene belatedly came to mind.
Yoo Sangah, who had happened to be standing in the direction I threw the cage. I thought I knew what she was thinking.
“It was just a coincidence. So it won't happen a second time.”
Yoo Sangah, nodding silently.
I couldn't tell what she was really thinking, but she was an intelligent woman, so she would have understood what I meant.
Because of my choice, someone had lived, and someone else had died.
Whoever the survivors were, I didn't deserve their thanks.
[Wow. Incredible.]
The dokkaebi appeared in midair with a crackle of static.
[What on earth happened here? I only stepped away to look at another carriage.......]
Delight and astonishment mingled on the dokkaebi's face.
Things resembling twinkling stars floated above its head.
I counted the stars to myself. One, two, three...... twenty, twenty-one. Twenty-one in all, then. No wonder it was pleased.

[A full twenty-one of you have joined my channel...... Haha, is this going to be my lucky day? Oh my, thank you for the donations, constellation-nims. Haha, everyone! Looks like you've earned your keep!]
The number of stars represented the number of constellations connected to the channel.
Twenty-one wasn't a large number, but it would be an unfamiliar one for a novice dokkaebi like this.
[Well, well, quite a few survivors, too! That guy in the next carriage was a lunatic as well...... You're making all sorts of interesting things happen today.]
Grinning, the dokkaebi manipulated something in midair. A moment later, a list of survivors appeared.
[Survivors of carriage 3807, Bulgwang-bound train 3434: Kim Dokja, Lee Hyunsung, Yoo Sangah, Han Myungoh, Lee Gilyoung. Total survivors: 5.]
5 people. More had survived than I expected.
I looked at the survivors' faces one by one.
I had expected the well-built, athletic Lee Hyunsung to survive. To some extent, I had expected Yoo Sangah to survive, too.
And Lee Gilyoung.
If my guess was right, ‘Lee Gilyoung’ would be the name of the boy standing beside me.
The boy's hand was smeared with fluid from a crushed grasshopper.
The grasshopper I had placed in his hand.
The boy, silently looking at his mother, whose head was gone.
His mother had abandoned him and joined in killing the old woman. And this boy had watched it all, from beginning to end.
After hesitating for a moment, I put a hand on his shoulder. It wasn't some pathetic act of sympathy.
If I had to put it into words, this was.......
Yes. Hypocrisy.
“Kid.”
The boy slowly raised his head. His eyes brimmed with the terror of death he had encountered for the first time in his life.
An unavoidable instinct.
Right now, this boy wasn't grieving his mother's death. He was simply afraid of his own. That was only natural. That was what it meant to be human.
“Do you want to live?”
The boy's pupils trembled with anxiety. His body shook as though resisting an irresistible force. Then his head moved, ever so slightly.
“Then come with me.”

Lee Gilyoung quietly moved closer and pressed himself against my leg. Yoo Sangah was looking at me as though she were moved. I was about to invite another unintended misunderstanding. To be fair, I had done it for an audience. Yoo Sangah just wasn't the audience I had in mind.
[A few constellations are moved by your good deed.]
[The constellations have donated 200 coins to you.]
Call it despicable, but I couldn't help it. I wanted to live, too.
Given the important event to come, attracting the constellations' attention now was essential.
“A-are you going to let us go now? Didn't we meet your conditions?”
Five or six steps away, Han Myungoh was shouting, his dress shirt torn into several strips.
Department Head Han Myungoh.
An absurdly lucky man.
But something puzzled me. Why had the wealthy Han Myungoh been riding the subway home from work?
The man who had recently made the rounds of every department, bragging that he'd bought a new Mercedes-Benz S-Class.
[Hmm, let you go? I take it you haven't had a proper look outside? Shall I really let you out?]
The dokkaebi snickered.
[Anyway, I'm impressed. I wasn't expecting much from this carriage, but you managed to pass the first scenario. You've proved that even insects deserve to survive.]
Those words brought our position home to me again. We probably looked like grasshoppers to that thing.

[Now, now, having overcome such hardship, you deserve a reward, don't you? As your reward for the first scenario, you've earned the right to receive sponsorship from none other than the ‘constellations’ themselves. Hooray! Well? Exciting, isn't it? Hmm, you're all rather indifferent. This really is a big deal.]
Really, that was inevitable.
I was the only person here who knew what ‘constellations’ or ‘sponsorship’ meant.
A constellation's sponsorship. What it meant was clear as day. <Sponsor Selection>, one of the key events in Ways of Survival, was finally about to begin.

[Hmm, you all look confused. Let me put it simply. Right now, you're very, pathetically weak. If I threw you into the scenario coming up next, forget a ‘Kruk’—even a puny ‘ground rat’ would kill you. But there are great beings in this universe who kindly take pity on you and wish to sponsor you. Do you understand?]
At last, unable to contain himself any longer, Lee Hyunsung spoke.
“What on earth do you mean? Who is sponsoring whom.......”

[Hmm, you really can't understand a fucking thing. There was a Korean proverb about this, wasn't there? Seeing once is better than hearing a hundred times. So experience it for yourselves. Well, the unlucky ones won't even get the chance. Hahaha!]
I tensed.
This was it.
I had to make a good choice here to make survival easier from now on.
“Dokja-ssi? Two strange options suddenly appeared. What on earth.......”
“Asking me won't help; I don't know either.”
Of course, that was a lie to avoid arousing unnecessary suspicion.
Still, two options.
Yoo Sangah was quite lucky, too.
“Let's take it easy. Think of it as an aptitude test.”
“An aptitude test.......”
“Nobody knows what's going on anyway. Wouldn't it be better to approach it with a calm mind?”
“Oh...... all right.”
Apparently thinking I was right, Yoo Sangah fell silent and began staring into the air. Her expression was deeply contemplative, as though she had received a strange fortune reading.
The others suddenly fell silent, too. They were probably all reading the options that had appeared before their eyes.
And I, too, was examining my options.
<Sponsor (背後) Selection>
―Choose your sponsor.
―Your chosen sponsor will become a dependable supporter.
1. Abyssal Black Flame Dragon
2. Demon-like Judge of Fire
3. Secretive Plotter
4. Prisoner of the Golden Headband
4 enigmatic options.
It meant a total of four constellations wanted to make me their incarnation (化身).
Considering that the protagonist of ‘Ways of Survival’ had initially received 5 options, 4 wasn't a small number.
Constellations never reveal their true names (眞名).
As a result, everyone entering a contract has to puzzle over cryptic metaphors such as ‘abyss,’ ‘demon,’ or ‘garden’ to infer a constellation's identity.
Of course, riddles like these were nothing to me, the sole reader of ‘Ways of Survival.’
Let's see.
First, ‘Abyssal Black Flame Dragon.’
As I recalled, this constellation was a powerful being who led a group of constellations called Black Cloud (黑雲).
I'd forgotten its true name, but I remembered it being very long.

The advantage of this constellation was the substantial boost to combat power that came with the contract. In particular, during the early stages, when boosts to Constitution and Strength were desperately needed, no constellation could match ‘Abyssal Black Flame Dragon.’
Of course, that only applied to the early stages.
The more frequently you used this constellation's power, the more your mind became corrupted, until you eventually became a murderer steeped in madness.
This constellation usually sponsored people with the ‘Chuunibyou’ attribute...... I didn't know why it had chosen me.
Something about it left a bad taste in my mouth, so I'd rule this one out for now.
Second, ‘Demon-like Judge of Fire.’
To think I'd actually get to see this option. For some reason, I was overwhelmed with emotion.
At first glance, this constellation seemed to reek of evil, but ‘demon-like’ was the trap. Put another way, ‘like a demon’ meant ‘definitely not a demon.’
Then you added the words ‘fire’ and ‘judgment.’
One who was not a demon, yet passed judgment through fire.
Paradoxically, the being behind this constellation was an angel.
If I remembered correctly, it was probably ‘Archangel Uriel’...... I remembered a character in the story choosing this constellation as their sponsor.
It was quite a good option, but I'd put this one on hold for now, too.
The formidable power of constellations aligned with Absolute Good (絕對善) came with absurd restrictions.
Third, ‘Secretive Plotter.’
Even I, an avid reader of Ways of Survival, had never seen this option before.
This might have been one of the constellations mentioned in passing...... but I couldn't tell at the moment. I felt I might get a sense of its identity if I read ‘Ways of Survival’ more closely.
One thing was certain: the being behind this constellation probably wasn't particularly powerful.
Even setting aside the weak adjective substituting for its true name, there wasn't a single proper noun.
Secretive Plotter—far too modest a modifier to represent a constellation. So this one went on hold, too.
Finally, ‘Prisoner of the Golden Headband.’
My heart pounded the moment I saw the fourth option.
To receive an offer from this constellation so early.
Several times, I wondered if my eyes were deceiving me, but there was no mistaking it.
It was unmistakably ‘Prisoner of the Golden Headband.’
At first glance, the word ‘prisoner’ gave this constellation a negative image, but the proper noun ‘Golden Headband’ was what you really needed to pay attention to.
The Golden Headband (緊箍兒).
The smallest prison in the world.
Anyone who had enjoyed reading Journey to the West as a child could easily recognize the clue.
Across all places and ages, there was only one prisoner bound by the Golden Headband.
The lord of Mount Huaguo, living in the agony of a shackle that tightened around his head. The Handsome Monkey King with Fiery Golden Eyes (火眼金睛).
The Great Sage, Heaven's Equal (齊天大聖), Sun Wukong.
Among the characters in the story, there was someone sponsored by this Great Sage, Heaven's Equal.
Wondrous power that swept away hundreds of incarnation bodies with a single swing of Ruyi and destroyed thousands of monsters with a single bolt of lightning.
The author had put a great deal of effort into the descriptions in that section, so I remembered it vividly.

I didn't know why this powerful constellation had taken an interest in me, but if I became the incarnation of the Great Sage, Heaven's Equal, I would be able to survive in this new world more easily than anyone else.
I quietly looked at the door connecting us to the carriage ahead.
I could vividly picture ‘that guy’ beyond the door, looking at a selection screen just as I was.
If I chose the ‘Great Sage, Heaven's Equal’...... could I beat him?
[1 minute remains until constellation sponsor selection ends.]
Time was running short.
I let out a light breath and looked over the options one last time.
I didn't deliberate for long.
[Sponsor Selection has ended.]
I took a deep breath as I watched the messages floating in the air.
[Several constellations are deeply shocked by your choice.]
Right. Now it begins.
[The constellation ‘Abyssal Black Flame Dragon’ is greatly enraged by your choice.]

[The constellations of Black Cloud (黑雲) are unsettled by the anger of ‘Abyssal Black Flame Dragon.’ You will not be able to receive sponsorship from constellations belonging to ‘Black Cloud’ for the time being.]
I'd expected this message, so I wasn't particularly surprised.

Making the entire gang turn their backs on me just because I'd rejected it······ I thought this had probably been Kim Namwoon's sponsor in the original novel. Like constellation, like incarnation, I supposed.
[The constellation ‘Demon-like Judge of Fire’ is disappointed in you.]
[She will persistently monitor your sense of justice from now on.]
Archangel Uriel's reaction stopped at disappointment. Constellations aligned with Absolute Good rarely hated anyone unless that person committed some tremendous injustice.
[The constellation ‘Secretive Plotter’ is intrigued by your choice.]
[200 coins have been donated.]
Secretive Plotter's reaction was completely unexpected. Judging by the nature I'd inferred from the adjective, I wondered if this constellation had appreciated my caution.
[The constellation ‘Prisoner of the Golden Headband’ is amused by your choice.]
And the Great Sage, Heaven's Equal······.
I began to feel conflicted.
Had I really made the right choice?
I didn't know.
Perhaps I had let an incredible opportunity slip away right before my eyes.
[You have not chosen a constellation sponsor.]
But choosing a constellation also meant placing a corresponding limit on my possibilities.
A contract with a constellation sponsor was never a fair ‘deal.’
I would survive.
But I wouldn't survive at the cost of becoming your plaything.
And if I was right, there was a way to grow stronger even without choosing a sponsor now.
A way to perhaps become even stronger than incarnations with the most powerful sponsors.
[Haha, well now······ Someone has made an interesting choice, haven't they? Well, all right. There will be other opportunities.]
The dokkaebi's eyes, curved like crescent moons, rested on me for a moment.
[Now, now, you should all have finished choosing, so take a little rest here. I need to go prepare the next scenario. See you in 10 minutes!]
After <Sponsor Selection> ended, the dokkaebi left us with that crap and disappeared.
It had told us to rest, but these 10 minutes were crucial.
Within 10 minutes, we had to sort all of this out and prepare for the next scenario.
I mentally went over the abilities I possessed.
[Character List], and [Omniscient Reader's Viewpoint].
I still didn't know exactly how to use them, but I had a rough idea of what kind of skills they were. With these, I could manage somehow.
“Everyone, please gather here.”
At my words, the survivors, who had been standing around watching one another uncertainly, gathered hesitantly. Lee Hyunsung was the first to extend a hand.
“Hello. I'm Lee Hyunsung.”
“I'm Kim Dokja.”
“I'm not sure ‘nice to meet you’··· is appropriate in this situation, but it's nice to meet you. As I mentioned, I'm a soldier······ though I suppose I should now say I was a soldier.”
“You can't get in touch with your unit?”
His grip was remarkably strong as we shook hands. Just what you'd expect from the tank in the early stages of ‘Ways of Survival,’ I supposed.
I had to take Lee Hyunsung with me.
He might not seem like much now, but Lee Hyunsung became increasingly important in the later parts of Ways of Survival.
“Oh, and Dokja-ssi.”
“Yes?”
“Thank you for earlier. If it hadn't been for you, we would all have died.”
“No, that's—”
“Or even if we'd survived, we couldn't have lived as human beings. Thank you so much. And······ I'm ashamed.”
Lee Hyunsung, bowing deeply at the waist.
I felt a little conflicted.
The truth was, Lee Hyunsung would have survived even if I hadn't done anything.
Someone grabbed my shoulder.
“Haha, our contract worker's done something big. Dokja-ssi, you know my name, don't you?”
I knew who it was without turning around. I removed the hand from my shoulder and said,
“I do, Han Myungoh-ssi.”
“Now, now, Han Myungoh-ssi? You should call me Department Head-nim, shouldn't you?”
Insisting on his rank even in this situation. Typical Han Myungoh.
Mino Soft's biggest old blowhard, and the final boss of authoritarianism.
“This isn't the office.”
“Ha, would you look at this. Planning to stop coming to work? Where did you learn such bad manners?”
Strangely, the sight of Han Myungoh snarling brought home once again that the world I had known was over.
Before the scenario began, the man before me had been a ‘predator’ in this world.
And I had been nothing more than prey before that predator. That was certainly how it had been.
“And no matter how I look at it, you went too far earlier. Huh? If you had bugs or something, you should at least have tipped me off. How could you throw them around so carelessly?”
“Kim Dokja-ssi, you'd better treat me well. Your contract's almost up, isn't it?”
Suddenly, it was funny.
So the world I'd lived in had been this fragile.
“Han Myungoh-ssi.”
“Huh?”
“Please shut up.”
“Wh-what?”

“Do you still not understand what's happening? Did that little shit need to beat you up earlier for you to come to your senses? Mino Soft? After all this, do you think a company like that still exists?”
Han Myungoh went pale, his mouth opening and closing.
I turned my gaze to the others. Now that I'd brought it up, I needed to make things clear.
“Han Myungoh-ssi isn't the only problem. Everyone, get a grip. As the dokkaebi said, this isn't a joke.”

“Even if you haven't said anything, I trust you've all worked out roughly what's happening. An Attributes Window, exclusive skills. An interface like a game's. Is there anyone who still doesn't get it?”
As expected, nobody raised a hand. This was what made Korea convenient. With smartphones so widespread, there was nobody who had never played an RPG.
Even if they hadn't played a phone game, they would at least have read a fantasy novel.
Lee Hyunsung sighed.
“This sort of thing only happened in the novels I read secretly while on duty. It still doesn't feel real. This really isn't a dream, is it?”
“Of course it's real.”
The look in Lee Hyunsung's eyes changed slightly at my composed reply.
[The character ‘Lee Hyunsung’ feels a faint sense of trust in you.]
[Your understanding of the character ‘Lee Hyunsung’ has increased.]
Lee Hyunsung nodded.
“I'm glad you're certain. Then what should we do now? Do you have any ideas, Dokja-ssi?”
“We need to get out of here.”
I spoke without the slightest hesitation.
“G-get out? Are you out of your mind?”
“Dokja-ssi, I also think that's a bit······.”
This time, even Yoo Sangah joined in.
They still hadn't come to their senses.
“Then how long do you plan to stay here?”
In fact, from a rational perspective, there was something unreasonable about what I was proposing. Outside was a paradise for monsters.
But I knew. We had to go outside now.
“Aren't you thinking about your parents? With all this happening, do you think they're safe?”
“Oh, actually, the phone hasn't been working for a while now. KakaoTalk isn't working either······.”
Yoo Sangah looked close to tears.
Just what you'd expect from Korea, where Confucianism still held strong. Everyone's face darkened at the single word ‘parents,’ even Lee Hyunsung's and Han Myungoh's.
I firmly squeezed the shoulder of Lee Gilyoung, who had his head bowed. Yoo Sangah was the first to rise.
“Let's go. We need to get out.”
“N-no! Didn't you hear what that bastard said? It told us to rest here! Our heads will burst if we go wandering around!”
“Let's take a majority vote.”
Yoo Sangah raised her hand first, followed by me and Lee Gilyoung. And that was all.
“······I do need to get back to my unit, but I think moving around carelessly in this situation would be dangerous. We were warned earlier, too.”
“Fuck, go out by yourselves! I'm not going! I said I'm not going!”
Han Myungoh was useless anyway, so he didn't matter. The problem was Lee Hyunsung. I had to bring him along somehow······.
Booom!
The thick steel plate buckled with a deafening crash. The steel door leading to carriage 3707 was slowly crumpling.
“Wh-what is that?”
Regardless of Han Myungoh's shouting, the steel door rang out with another crash.
Booom!
Someone on the other side was trying to break down the steel door. This was unexpected, and my thoughts raced.
Could this be the next scenario?
No. The dokkaebi wasn't back yet.
My mind worked quickly.
The fine hairs on my skin stood up, and a brief shudder ran through my entire body.
It was him.
“Wh-what are you doing? Everyone, block the door!”
Han Myungoh shouted as he backed away from the door. I stopped Lee Hyunsung from approaching it.
“You won't be able to stop him.”
“Pardon?”
“We need to get out of here right now.”
I spoke as I stared grimly at the steel door.
“What? But—”
“If we don't leave now―”
The sole survivor of carriage 3707. The identity of the person beyond that door was all too obvious.
“We'll all die before the next scenario even arrives.”
Yes. He was finally coming.
The ‘real’ protagonist of this story.
I looked straight into the eyes of the hesitant Lee Hyunsung and Han Myungoh and said,
“Die here at the hands of the guy beyond that steel door, or get out of the train and try your luck. Which will you choose?”
“Dokja-ssi, there's no guarantee that whoever's beyond that steel door is an enemy, is there?”
The Steel Sword Emperor faltered at crucial moments. There was a reason Lee Hyunsung couldn't be the party leader.
“If they're coming from another carriage, they're likely a survivor. We could at least meet them······.”
Instead of answering, I surveyed the blood-soaked carriage. Lee Hyunsung followed my gaze and quietly closed his mouth.
“······I spoke thoughtlessly. Let's find a way out.”
“L-let's go! Let's get out, quickly!”
In that instant, the two of them had realized it, too.
That the survivors in the other carriages must have been through the same thing we had.
And that they wouldn't have been lucky enough to have ‘insects.’
“This one's broken!”
“Damn it, this one won't turn, either!”
Listening to Lee Hyunsung's and Han Myungoh's shouts, I checked a door mechanism myself. I could now touch the mechanism that had been sealed behind a barrier earlier.
Excluding the doors connecting the carriages, a subway carriage had 8 entry doors in total. And 3 exits remained unchecked.
Boom!
The steel door looked unlikely to last even another minute.
Protagonist or not, his Strength level couldn't be high enough at this early stage. Frankly, it was astonishing that he would even think of breaking down that thick steel door.
“Dokja-ssi! Here―”
We had found a working manual door mechanism.
“I'm opening it!”
But although the mechanism turned smoothly, the door didn't open all the way. About a fifth of the way open, it stopped as though caught on something.
“······This one seems to be broken, too.”
“What about the others?”
“This is the only one we have any chance of getting through.”
A child might manage it, but the gap was too narrow for an adult man or woman. Han Myungoh and Lee Hyunsung each grabbed one side of the door and strained with all their might, but it didn't budge.
[Coins held: 4700 C]
One use for coins was raising overall stats.
I'd already spent 2700 coins bringing my Constitution level to 10.
If I used the remaining coins to raise my Strength level, I could somehow solve this, but with no way of knowing what might happen or when, I couldn't spend coins recklessly at this early stage.
In the end, there was only one approach I could count on.
“Lee Hyunsung-ssi. Use your skill.”
“Pardon? By skill, you mean······.”
I quietly activated [Character List].
[The exclusive skill ‘Character List’ activates.]
<Character Information>
Name: Lee Hyunsung
Age: 28
Constellation Sponsor (背後星): Master of Steel
Exclusive Attribute: Soldier who Turned a Blind Eye to Injustice (General)
Exclusive Skills: [Bayonet Skills Lv.2], [Camouflage Lv.2], [Patience Lv.2]
Stigma: [Great Mountain Push Lv.1]
Overall Stats: [Constitution Lv.8], [Strength Lv.8], [Agility Lv.7], [Magic Power Lv.5]
Overall Evaluation: His overall stats are very good. Despite tolerating injustice remarkably well, he has been chosen by a constellation. This will give him another opportunity.
Lee Hyunsung's information appeared before my eyes without any restrictions. Fortunately, both his chosen sponsor and his attribute were exactly as I had read in the book.
“You must have checked when you opened your Attributes Window earlier. Since you're a soldier, Lee Hyunsung-ssi, you should have at least one skill useful in this situation.”
“Well··· I do have one, but I don't know how to use it―”
“Just think to yourself that you're using that skill.”
“······That's all it takes?”
“Yes. I tried it myself earlier.”
Lee Hyunsung looked doubtful, then drew a heavy breath as though making up his mind.
“Haaaaaah!”
As Lee Hyunsung gripped the door, his biceps swelled as though they might burst. It seemed [Great Mountain Push] had activated successfully.
Strictly speaking, [Great Mountain Push] was actually a ‘stigma (星痕),’ not a skill. And a stigma was power received from a constellation sponsor.
I had deliberately called it a ‘skill’ to avoid suspicion.
Rrrrrrr.
There was a sound like a giant clockwork spring being wound, and at last the door began to move.
“What the! This fellow's a real strongman!”
“It worked! It really worked!”
[The character ‘Lee Hyunsung’ begins to trust you.]
[Your understanding of the character ‘Lee Hyunsung’ has increased.]
Far from becoming suspicious, his trust had increased. At times like this, Lee Hyunsung was simpler than I'd thought.
“Let's get off. Hurry!”
But it was too early to relax. I lifted Lee Gilyoung and handed him to Lee Hyunsung.
“Lee Hyunsung-ssi. Carry the child on your back.”
“Understood.”
The steel door was almost completely broken down now. But if I was right, that door wasn't our immediate problem.
[······Well, now. I knew this would happen. Didn't I tell you earlier? Not to go anywhere. Damn it! I'm not done preparing the scenario yet―]
The dokkaebi hovered above Dongho Bridge, looking angry.
“Aaah! I knew this would happen! I told you we shouldn't come out!”
Apparently thinking his head would burst, Han Myungoh clutched his temples. But he was worrying for nothing.
[Whew······ Well, it can't be helped. You really are lucky humans.]
Because the ‘second scenario’ began the very moment we opened the train door.
[The second scenario has arrived!]
<Sub-scenario - Escape>
Category: Sub
Difficulty: E
Clear Condition: Cross the broken bridge and enter Oksu Station.
Time Limit: 20 minutes
Reward: 200 coins
On Failure: ???
“Dokja-ssi, something's strange. It says ‘broken bridge,’ but the bridge is still······.”
“Don't worry about it. Run! Hurry!”
“O-okay!”
Yoo Sangah's observation was correct.
The bridge hadn't broken yet.
Put another way, that meant ‘the bridge would definitely break.’
“Hurry and come along too, Dokja-ssi!”
“I'm coming.”
The bridge hadn't broken yet because we had gotten off the train ‘too early.’
The dokkaebi had said it needed 10 minutes to prepare. But we had escaped a full 3 minutes before that.
You could call it cowardly, but this scenario was impossible to clear without a trick like that.
